title: The Broken Mile
subtitle: VR fiber-optic field training deployed via ArborXR, published on the Meta Quest Store.

hero.label: VR ENVIRONMENT SCENE · FIBER SPLICE BAY

overview.label: 01 — Overview
overview.body: Millennium needed field technicians trained on fiber-optic splicing and fault diagnosis without pulling them off paying jobs or risking live customer equipment. The Broken Mile puts them inside a full VR fiber cabinet to run a real troubleshooting job start to finish, as many times as it takes. Deployed via ArborXR and published on the Meta Quest Store.

problem.label: 02 — The Problem
problem.quote: "You can't practice on a live line."
problem.body: Field techs learned splicing by shadowing senior technicians and by trial and error on real customer equipment — expensive when it went wrong, and inconsistent as a way to build judgment. Millennium needed a way for techs to fail safely, as many times as it took.
problem.mediaLabel: TRAINING GAP: CURRENT VS. NEEDED STATE

process.name: Task Mapping
process.body: Shadowed field technicians to map the real troubleshooting sequence step-by-step.

process.name: Environment & Interaction
process.body: Built the fiber cabinet and the hand-tracked splice interactions that stand in for the real tool.

process.name: Instructional Scaffolding
process.body: Layered guided and free-play modes so skill-builds fold in stages, not all at once.

process.name: Deployment & QA
process.body: Packaged for ArborXR fleet management and passed Meta Quest Store certification.

finalDesign.label: 05 — Final Design
cards: The full fiber cabinet environment, built to match the real-world equipment layouts.
Hand-tracked splice interaction — guided vs. intuitive capture.
Guided vs. Free-play mode selection screens.
Published training on the Meta Quest Store.

outcomes.label: 06 — Outcomes
items: Published on the Meta Quest Store and deployed via ArborXR to Millennium's field technician onboarding.
Replaced live equipment shadowing with a repeatable, fail-safe practice environment.

reflection.label: 07 — Reflection
reflection.quote: Designing for safety-critical, hands-on skills meant the interactive fidelity had to feel like the real tool, not a simplified stand-in — every splice, every fault, had to be trustworthy enough that the learning actually transferred to the field.
